subQuestions.questionText: The part in the alimentary canal of fowls which is the common opening for the digestive and urogenital systems:
subQuestions.memoText:
Correct answer: D (2 marks)
The cloaca is the common opening for the digestive and urogenital systems in fowls.

subQuestions.questionText: The energy value of a feed that is calculated by subtracting energy lost through faeces, urine and gases from gross energy:
subQuestions.memoText:
Correct answer: C (2 marks)
Metabolic energy is calculated by subtracting energy lost through faeces, urine and gases from gross energy.

subQuestions.questionText: … are volatile fatty acids that are the end products of microbial fermentation in the rumen.
subQuestions.memoText:
Correct answer: B (2 marks)
Acetic and propionic acid are volatile fatty acids produced as end products of microbial fermentation in the rumen.

subQuestions.questionText:
Micro-organisms in ruminant animals have the following functions:
(i) The digestion of vitamin A and K
(ii) The synthesis of amino acids
(iii) The hydrolysis of protein
(iv) Conversion of ammonia to high-quality microbial protein
Choose the CORRECT combination:
subQuestions.memoText:
Correct answer: C (2 marks)
(ii), (iii) and (iv) - Micro-organisms in ruminants synthesize amino acids, hydrolyse protein, and convert ammonia to high-quality microbial protein. They synthesize (not digest) vitamins.

subQuestions.questionText: The following should be considered to avoid stress and aggressive behaviour in male farm animals:
subQuestions.memoText:
Correct answer: C (2 marks)
Grouping animals that are familiar with one another and of the same age together helps avoid stress and aggressive behaviour.

options.A: House all male farm animals in one pen.
options.B: Place male animals together regardless of their body weight and age.
options.C: Group animals that are familiar with one another and of the same age together.
options.D: Place male and female animals together during the breeding season.

subQuestions.questionText: ONE of the following is a basic guideline to be considered when transporting animals:
subQuestions.memoText:
Correct answer: A (2 marks)
Pregnant animals should not be transported to avoid stress, injury, and abortion risks.

options.A: Pregnant animals should not be transported.
options.B: Transport cattle, sheep and goats together in an unpartitioned truck.
options.D: Feed animals immediately before they are loaded.

subQuestions.questionText: The … is NOT a principle of good health to control diseases and parasites in farm animals.
subQuestions.memoText:
Correct answer: B (2 marks)
Retention of manure in the broiler house is NOT a principle of good health - manure should be removed regularly to prevent disease and parasite buildup.

options.A: disinfecting of shelters and feed containers
options.B: retention of manure in the broiler house
options.C: isolation of animals with contagious diseases
options.D: use of the correct application technique and dosage of medication

subQuestions.questionText:
The following are signs of an animal with poor health:
(i) Discoloured urine
(ii) Loss of appetite and weight
(iii) Smooth and shiny hair coat in cattle
(iv) Isolation from the rest of the herd
Choose the CORRECT combination:
subQuestions.memoText:
Correct answer: D (2 marks)
(i), (ii) and (iv) - Discoloured urine, loss of appetite/weight, and isolation are signs of poor health. A smooth shiny coat indicates good health.

subQuestions.questionText: The following may cause abortion, except for …
subQuestions.memoText:
Correct answer: B (2 marks)
Embryo normality does NOT cause abortion. Strong laxatives, toxic elements in feed, and injuries can all cause abortion.

subQuestions.questionText: When the signs of oestrus are observed in the morning, the best time to administer artificial insemination is …
subQuestions.memoText:
Correct answer: A (2 marks)
12 hours later in the afternoon - This timing maximizes the chance of conception based on ovulation timing relative to oestrus signs.

subQuestions.questionText: Indicate whether the description applies to A only, B only, both A and B or none. COLUMN A: A: Duodenum; B: Jejunum. COLUMN B: The part where maximum absorption of nutrients occurs.
subQuestions.memoText:
Correct answer: B only (2 marks)
Maximum absorption of nutrients occurs in the jejunum, not the duodenum.

subQuestions.questionText: Indicate whether the description applies to A only, B only, both A and B or none. COLUMN A: A: Urea; B: Biuret. COLUMN B: A non-protein nitrogen substance that is safer to use because it is less soluble.
subQuestions.memoText:
Correct answer: B only (2 marks)
Biuret is a non-protein nitrogen substance that is safer to use because it is less soluble than urea.

subQuestions.questionText: Indicate whether the description applies to A only, B only, both A and B or none. COLUMN A: A: Balling guns; B: Drenching guns. COLUMN B: Tools that farmers use for the castration of farm animals.
subQuestions.memoText:
Correct answer: None (2 marks)
Neither balling guns nor drenching guns are used for castration. Both are used for administering medication.

subQuestions.questionText: Indicate whether the description applies to A only, B only, both A and B or none. COLUMN A: A: Watery diarrhoea; B: Bottle-jaw. COLUMN B: Visible symptoms of roundworm infestation in farm animals.
subQuestions.memoText:
Correct answer: Both A and B (2 marks)
Both watery diarrhoea and bottle-jaw are visible symptoms of roundworm infestation in farm animals.

subQuestions.questionText: Indicate whether the description applies to A only, B only, both A and B or none. COLUMN A: A: Embryo splitting; B: Embryo flushing. COLUMN B: Method used to separate the embryos to increase the number of offspring during embryo transplant.
subQuestions.memoText:
Correct answer: A only (2 marks)
Embryo splitting is the method used to separate the embryos to increase the number of offspring during embryo transplant.

subQuestions.questionText: Give ONE word/term: A measure of the digestibility of a feed which is expressed as a percentage of the dry matter.
subQuestions.memoText: Answer: Digestibility coefficient (2 marks)

subQuestions.questionText: Give ONE word/term: An organism that carries a disease from one animal to another.
subQuestions.memoText: Answer: Vector (2 marks)

subQuestions.questionText: Give ONE word/term: Oval projections in the uterus walls that provide future attachment to the foetus.
subQuestions.memoText: Answer: Caruncles/nodules (2 marks)

subQuestions.questionText: Give ONE word/term: The embryonic membrane that forms a sac filled with a fluid that acts as a shock absorber to protect the embryo.
subQuestions.memoText: Answer: Amnion (2 marks)

subQuestions.questionText: Give ONE word/term: A tool that consists of a rectal probe and is used to collect semen.
subQuestions.memoText: Answer: Electro ejaculator (2 marks)

subQuestions.questionText: Change the UNDERLINED WORD(S) to make the statement TRUE: Mineral lick is a method of supplementing minerals where an animal takes in as much minerals as required.
subQuestions.memoText:
Answer: Cafeteria style/free choice/ad lib (1 mark)
The correct term is cafeteria style (or free choice/ad lib) feeding, where the animal takes in as much minerals as required.

subQuestions.questionText: Change the UNDERLINED WORD(S) to make the statement TRUE: Marbling is the stiffening of muscles in the body of an animal immediately after slaughtering.
subQuestions.memoText:
Answer: Rigor mortis (1 mark)
Rigor mortis is the stiffening of muscles after slaughter; marbling refers to fat distribution in muscle.

subQuestions.questionText: Change the UNDERLINED WORD(S) to make the statement TRUE: Flushing is the release of a large number of ova at the same time.
subQuestions.memoText:
Answer: Super ovulation (1 mark)
Super ovulation is the release of a large number of ova at the same time; flushing is high-energy feeding before mating.

subQuestions.questionText: Change the UNDERLINED WORD(S) to make the statement TRUE: The endometria are paired tubes that transport ova from the ovaries to the uterus.
subQuestions.memoText:
Answer: Fallopian tubes/oviducts (1 mark)
The fallopian tubes (oviducts) transport ova from the ovaries to the uterus; the endometrium is the uterine lining.

subQuestions.questionText: Change the UNDERLINED WORD(S) to make the statement TRUE: A hormone secreted by the Graafian follicle which is responsible for the onset of oestrus is progesterone.
subQuestions.memoText:
Answer: Oestrogen (1 mark)
Oestrogen is secreted by the Graafian follicle and is responsible for the onset of oestrus; progesterone maintains pregnancy.

subQuestions.questionText: The diagrams show parts of the stomachs of two farm animals. Identify the diagram (A or B) that represents the stomach of an adult ruminant animal. (Refer to the diagram in the question paper showing Diagram A with oesophageal groove and abomasum, and Diagram B with reticulum, omasum, and abomasum.)
subQuestions.memoText: Answer: Diagram B (1 mark)

subQuestions.questionText: Justify the answer to QUESTION 2.1.1.
subQuestions.memoText:
Any 1 of the following (1 mark):
• Presence of a large rumen in relation to the abomasum
• Presence of a smaller abomasum in relation to rumen
• Fully developed fore-stomach
• Absence of the oesophageal groove

subQuestions.questionText: State the function of the oesophageal groove.
subQuestions.memoText:
Answer (1 mark):
It channels milk to pass from the oesophagus to the abomasum.

subQuestions.questionText: Identify the part of the stomach in DIAGRAM B that performs the same function as the proventriculus in poultry.
subQuestions.memoText: Answer: Abomasum (1 mark)

subQuestions.questionText:
The table shows information on the sizes of the stomachs in sheep at different ages:
Birth: Reticulorumen 30%, Abomasum 60%
1 month: Reticulorumen 60%, Abomasum 30%
2 months: Reticulorumen 80%, Abomasum 20%
3 months: Reticulorumen 70%, Abomasum 15%
Adult: Reticulorumen 70%, Abomasum 10%
Draw a combined bar graph to show the size of the reticulorumen and abomasum in sheep at different ages by using the data in the table above.
subQuestions.memoText:
Marking criteria (6 marks - 1 mark each):
• Correct heading (with both variables) - e.g. 'Size of the reticulorumen and abomasum in sheep at different ages'
• X-axis: Correctly calibrated with label (Age)
• Y-axis: Correctly calibrated with label (Size)
• Correct units (% of the total stomach)
• Combined bar graph (both bars side by side for each age)
• Accuracy (80% + correctly plotted)

subQuestions.questionText: The graph shows the composition of a ration for farm animals (Lucerne hay ~65kg, Soyabean oilcake meal ~21kg, Wheat meal ~45kg, Molasses ~30kg, Urea ~5kg). Indicate the type of farm animal that CANNOT benefit from the ration presented in the graph above.
subQuestions.memoText: Answer: Non-ruminant/monogastric (1 mark)

subQuestions.questionText: Give a reason to support the answer to QUESTION 2.3.1 based on the composition of the ration.
subQuestions.memoText:
Any 1 of the following (2 marks - 1 for identifying component, 1 for explanation):
• The ration contains high quantities of roughage/hay which cannot be digested by non-ruminants
• The ration contains urea which cannot be digested by non-ruminants

subQuestions.questionText:
Identify a feed in the graph above that is an example of EACH of the following:
(a) Protein-rich roughage
(b) Carbohydrate-rich concentrate
subQuestions.memoText:
Answers (2 marks - 1 mark each):
(a) Protein-rich roughage: Lucerne hay
(b) Carbohydrate-rich concentrate: Wheat meal

subQuestions.questionText: Calculate the dry matter content of the feed in kg if an animal ingested 25 kg of a feed containing 15% moisture. Show ALL calculations.
subQuestions.memoText:
Any 2 marks of the following:
Method 1:
Mark 1: $25 \text{ kg} \times 0.15 = 3.75 \text{ kg}$ OR $\frac{15}{100} \times 25 = 3.75 \text{ kg}$
Mark 2: $25 \text{ kg} - 3.75 \text{ kg} = 21.25 \text{ kg}$

OR Method 2:
Mark 1: $\frac{85}{100} \times 25 \text{ kg}$
Mark 2: $= 21.25 \text{ kg}$

subQuestions.questionText: A farmer mixed oatmeal and fishmeal to prepare a ration containing 14% digestible protein (DP). The oatmeal contains 12% DP and fishmeal 28% DP. Use the Pearson square method to calculate the ratio at which oatmeal and fishmeal will be mixed.
subQuestions.memoText:
Pearson Square (4 marks):
Mark 1: Oatmeal: 12% DP shown on top-left
Mark 2: Fishmeal: 28% DP shown on bottom-left
Mark 3: 14% (desired DP) in centre of square
Mark 4: Calculations of differences:
  - Top right (oatmeal parts): $|28 - 14| = 14$ parts
  - Bottom right (fishmeal parts): $|12 - 14| = 2$ parts

Ratio: Oatmeal to fishmeal = 14 : 2 / Fishmeal to oatmeal = 2 : 14

subQuestions.questionText: Calculate the percentage of fishmeal in the mixture.
subQuestions.memoText:
Marks (3 marks - 1 mark each):
Mark 1: Total parts = $2 + 14 = 16$
Mark 2: $\frac{2}{16} \times 100$
Mark 3: $= 12.5\%$

subQuestions.questionText:
The table shows nutrients available in two different feeds:
Feed A: Carbohydrates 61%, Digestible Protein 17%, Fats 5%, Nutritive Ratio ...
Feed B: Carbohydrates 74%, Digestible Protein 9%, Fats 7%, Nutritive Ratio 1:9
Identify, in the table above, the feed that is suitable for each of the following:
(a) Fattening of lambs
(b) Lactating cows
subQuestions.memoText:
Answers (2 marks - 1 mark each):
(a) Fattening of lambs: FEED B
(b) Lactating cows: FEED A

subQuestions.questionText: Justify, with a reason, the answer to QUESTION 2.6.1(b).
subQuestions.memoText:
Answer (1 mark):
Feed A is high in protein content / has a high digestible protein of 17% which is needed for milk production in lactating cows.

subQuestions.questionText: Calculate the nutritive ratio of FEED A. Show ALL calculations, including the formula.
subQuestions.memoText:
Marks (3 marks - 1 mark each):
Method 1:
Mark 1: Formula: $NR = 1 : \frac{\%TDN - \%DP}{\%DP}$
Mark 2: $= 1 : \frac{83\% - 17\%}{17\%}$
Mark 3: $= 1 : 3.9$ or $1 : 4$

OR Method 2:
Mark 1: Formula: $NR = 1 : \frac{\%DNNS}{\%DP}$
Mark 2: $= 1 : \frac{66\%}{17\%}$
Mark 3: $= 1 : 3.9$ or $1 : 4$

subQuestions.questionText: The schematic representation illustrates two feed components, the enzymes and the end products of the digestion of the feed components. (Refer to the schematic in the question paper showing: Dry matter of feed → Inorganic components and Organic components → A, Lipids → Cellulose, Starch, Fats and oils → enzymes B (Cellulase), C, → Nutrients D, E, Fatty acids and glycerol). Identify A and E.
subQuestions.memoText:
Answers (2 marks - 1 mark each):
A - Carbohydrates
E - Maltose/glucose
subQuestions.topic: Animal Nutrition - Feed Components and Digestion

subQuestions.questionText: Name the enzyme represented by C that acts on fats and oils.
subQuestions.memoText:
Answer (1 mark):
C - Lipase

subQuestions.questionText:
Name a feed component for each of the following:
(a) An organic component other than those in the schematic representation
(b) Inorganic component
subQuestions.memoText:
Answers (2 marks - 1 mark each):
(a) Other organic component: Vitamin / Protein
(b) Inorganic component: Minerals

subQuestions.questionText:
The table shows two farmers involved in farming activities. FARMER A: A farmer has one worker and 58 goats, which depend on natural pastures in a large communal land. Goats are kept in a kraal at night and get water from a stream. FARMER B: A farmer keeps 540 sheep on 30 ha land, 9 workers, 2 boreholes, 2 feed sheds, a feedlot and a sheep handling facility. The farmer buys feeds and also grows lucerne. Identify the production system practised by each of the following:
(a) FARMER B
(b) FARMER A
subQuestions.memoText:
Answers (2 marks - 1 mark each):
(a) FARMER B - Intensive
(b) FARMER A - Extensive

subQuestions.questionText: Give TWO reasons in the table above to support the answer to QUESTION 3.1.1(a).
subQuestions.memoText:
Any 2 of the following (2 marks):
• Animals are provided with feed
• Many workers / 9 workers
• High stock density / 540 sheep on 30 ha
• More capital invested / feedlot / housing / 2 feed sheds / 2 boreholes

subQuestions.questionText: State TWO factors that FARMER A should consider in order to increase production of the farm animals.
subQuestions.memoText:
Any 2 of the following (2 marks):
• Nutrition / feeding
• Breeding / reproduction
• Environment / shelter
• Management

subQuestions.questionText:
The picture shows a housing facility for pigs with labels A (a roof structure), B (Straw), and C (an outdoor area). Identify the letter (A to C) that represents the structure, equipment or material that is BEST suited to each of the following statements:
(a) Protects pigs against radiation during the day
(b) Keeps pigs dry and warm at night
(c) An area where pigs can roam freely during the day
subQuestions.memoText:
Answers (3 marks - 1 mark each):
(a) A (the roof - protects from solar radiation)
(b) B (the straw - bedding to keep dry and warm)
(c) C (the outdoor area - for roaming)

subQuestions.questionText: The picture shows the handling of a chick (a chick being injected with a syringe). Identify the reason for handling a chick as indicated in the picture above.
subQuestions.memoText:
Answer (1 mark):
Application of medication / vaccinating / immunising / inoculating

subQuestions.questionText: Name the tool used in the picture above.
subQuestions.memoText:
Answer (1 mark):
Syringe

subQuestions.questionText: Indicate TWO basic guidelines for handling poultry.
subQuestions.memoText:
Any 2 of the following (2 marks):
• Approach the birds in a quiet, easy moving manner that does not raise alarm / do not chase chickens around
• Carry them by both legs or wings
• Never carry them by head, one wing/leg
• Do not grab chickens by the feathers/tail

subQuestions.questionText: Name TWO types of equipment or tools that are used by farmers to restrain farm animals.
subQuestions.memoText:
Any 2 of the following (2 marks):
• Crush / head gate / neck clamp / chute / race
• Tilting / restraining table
• Rope
• Harness
• Halter
• Nose ring / nose pliers

subQuestions.questionText: Indicate the method of administering medication: Treatment of external parasites by immersing farm animals in water mixed with a pesticide.
subQuestions.memoText:
Answer (1 mark):
Plunge dipping

subQuestions.questionText: Indicate the method of administering medication: Administering liquid medication through the mouth to treat internal parasites.
subQuestions.memoText:
Answer (1 mark):
Dosing / drenching

subQuestions.questionText: Indicate the method of administering medication: The insertion of drugs to prevent infections that may be caused by retained placenta.
subQuestions.memoText:
Answer (1 mark):
Vaginal insertion

subQuestions.questionText: Indicate the method of administering medication: Treatment of wounds on the skin of a farm animal.
subQuestions.memoText:
Answer (1 mark):
Topical administration

subQuestions.questionText:
Name the animal disease described by EACH of the following statements:
(a) Swelling in the lower body region, a bloody discharge from the body openings, staggering, trembling, difficult breathing and convulsive movements
(b) Causes a high temperature in animals followed by the development of blisters mainly in the mouth and on the feet
(c) Is caused by single-celled parasites resulting in watery diarrhoea, mucus, blood in the droppings and whitish soiling around the vent
(d) A disease that affects the skin causing hard scab masses that lift from the skin with the fleece as the disease grows
subQuestions.memoText:
Answers (4 marks - 1 mark each):
(a) Anthrax
(b) Foot & Mouth Disease (FMD)
(c) Coccidiosis
(d) Lumpy wool

subQuestions.questionText:
Indicate the pathogen that causes the disease named in EACH of the following questions:
(a) 3.5.1(d)
(b) 3.5.1(a)
subQuestions.memoText:
Answers (2 marks - 1 mark each):
(a) 3.5.1(d) [Lumpy wool] - Fungi / Dermatophilus congolensis / Pseudomonas aeruginosa
(b) 3.5.1(a) [Anthrax] - Bacteria / Bacillus anthracis

subQuestions.questionText: The diagram shows the life cycle of a parasite (showing animal getting infected, eggs in dung, miracidia hatching from eggs, larval stage in snail, cercariae, metacercariae encysting on grass). Name the parasite in the diagram above.
subQuestions.memoText:
Answer (1 mark):
Liver fluke

subQuestions.questionText:
Identify EACH of the following in the diagram:
(a) Primary host
(b) Secondary host
subQuestions.memoText:
Answers (2 marks - 1 mark each):
(a) Primary host: Cattle/sheep
(b) Secondary host: Snail

subQuestions.questionText: State a measure a farmer can adopt to break the life cycle of the parasite named in QUESTION 3.6.1 and prevent further infestation.
subQuestions.memoText:
Any 1 of the following (1 mark):
• Keep animals away from wet pastures
• Practice rotational grazing

subQuestions.questionText: The table shows different parasites that affect farm animals: PARASITE A: Lays eggs on wool that is soiled with faeces and also on open wounds. PARASITE B: Causes irritation of the sinuses, sneezing and severe nasal discharge. PARASITE C: Causes skin irritation with severe itching resulting in mange. Classify the parasites in the table above.
subQuestions.memoText:
Answer (1 mark):
External / ecto parasites

subQuestions.questionText: Identify PARASITE A and PARASITE C.
subQuestions.memoText:
Answers (2 marks - 1 mark each):
PARASITE A - Blowfly
PARASITE C - Mite

subQuestions.questionText: State ONE management practice to prevent infestation by PARASITE A.
subQuestions.memoText:
Any 1 of the following (1 mark):
• Clipping and cleaning of coat
• Timing the shearing and crutching of wool
• Tail docking
• Lambing should be after shearing
• Breeding of resistant animals
• Proper waste management / judicious blowfly control measures
• Keep the living areas of animals clean
• Treat / cover open wounds

subQuestions.questionText: Urea poisoning occurs when animals consume too much of it. Name ONE symptom of urea poisoning in farm animals.
subQuestions.memoText:
Any 1 of the following (1 mark):
• Bloating
• Tetany / painful muscular cramps
• Difficult / rapid breathing
• Excessive salivation
• Frequent defaecation
• Constipation
• Staggering
• Nervous symptoms

subQuestions.questionText: Indicate a method the farmer can use to treat urea poisoning in farm animals.
subQuestions.memoText:
Any 1 of the following (1 mark):
• Removal of animals from the source of poisoning
• Administer vinegar / acetic acid to neutralise the ammonia (dilute one litre of vinegar with four litres of water using stomach tube)
• Administer large amounts of cold water to dilute the rumen content and slow the rate of urease activity

subQuestions.questionText: The diagram shows the reproductive system of a male farm animal with labels A, B, C, D, E (Seminiferous tubules), F, G, and Retractor muscle. Name structures A and D.
subQuestions.memoText:
Answers (2 marks - 1 mark each):
A - Cowper's glands / bulbo-urethral glands
D - Vas deferens / sperm duct / ductus deferens / seminal tube

subQuestions.questionText:
Write down the letter that represents the part that is responsible for EACH of the following functions:
(a) Secretion of milky alkaline mucus that gives semen its characteristic smell
(b) Production of male sex hormones
(c) Provision of energy and more fluid to increase volume of semen
(d) Storage of spermatozoa until maturity
(e) Regulation of the temperature of the testes
subQuestions.memoText:
Answers (5 marks - 1 mark each):
(a) B (Prostate gland)
(b) E (Testis)
(c) C (Seminal vesicles)
(d) F (Epididymis)
(e) G (Scrotum/cremaster muscle)

subQuestions.questionText: State TWO factors that cause sterility in bulls.
subQuestions.memoText:
Any 2 of the following (2 marks):
• Deformed reproductive organs
• Diseases
• Congenital defects (hypoplasia / cryptorchidism / hermaphroditism)
• Genetic defects
• Azoospermia

subQuestions.questionText: The illustration shows the process of gametogenesis in female farm animals (showing Oogonium → Maturation (A) → labelled cell B → splits into Secondary oocyte and First polar body (C) → Secondary oocyte splits into Ootid and Second polar body (D) → Ootid undergoes Differentiation → cell E). Identify the type of gametogenesis represented by the illustration above.
subQuestions.memoText:
Answer (1 mark):
Oogenesis / ovigenesis

subQuestions.questionText: Label B and E.
subQuestions.memoText:
Answers (2 marks - 1 mark each):
B - Primary oocyte
E - Ovum / egg cell

subQuestions.questionText:
Name the type of cell division represented by EACH of the following:
(a) A
(b) D
subQuestions.memoText:
Answers (2 marks - 1 mark each):
(a) A - Mitosis
(b) D - II Meiotic division (Meiosis II)

subQuestions.questionText: Hormones are used by farmers to bring female animals to oestrus at approximately the same time. Identify the reproductive technique indicated by the statement above.
subQuestions.memoText:
Answer (1 mark):
Synchronisation of oestrus

subQuestions.questionText: State TWO disadvantages of the reproductive technique in QUESTION 4.3.1.
subQuestions.memoText:
Any 2 of the following (2 marks):
• Requires high levels of technology
• Conditions such as poor nutrition and poor health may affect oestrus synchronisation negatively
• High labour costs during heat detection / high costs for good facilities / expensive
• Time intensive

subQuestions.questionText: The diagram shows the reproductive technique that takes place in female animals (showing a person's hand inserting a pistollete into the body of the uterus). Identify the reproductive technique represented in the diagram above.
subQuestions.memoText:
Answer (1 mark):
Artificial Insemination / AI

subQuestions.questionText: State TWO advantages of the reproductive technique identified in QUESTION 4.4.1.
subQuestions.memoText:
Any 2 of the following (2 marks):
• Reduces sexually transmitted diseases
• Cost effective / cheaper than maintaining bulls / no need to buy expensive bulls
• Semen of one bull can be used to inseminate many cows
• Rapid method to improve the quality of the herd
• Imported semen can be used
• Valuable tool in assisting with progeny testing / improves the genetic value of the herd
• Higher conception rate than with natural mating
• Can be applied where mating is impossible
• Can be used long after the death of the bull

subQuestions.questionText: State ONE basic requirement for semen collection.
subQuestions.memoText:
Any 1 of the following (1 mark):
• Hygienic conditions / sterile equipment
• Semen collection point should be closer to laboratory
• Male animal should be healthy and clean
• Collection vial must be warmed
• Equipment must be readily available
• The floor should not be slippery
• Presence of a teaser animal
• Experienced / skilled personnel

subQuestions.questionText: State ONE characteristic of high quality semen.
subQuestions.memoText:
Any 1 of the following (1 mark):
• It must be viable / less than 15% dead sperm cells
• Semen should be milky / opaque in colour
• Sticky with a characteristic smell
• No blood in the semen
• Sperm cells should have normal morphology / not deformed
• High concentration semen
• High mobility of sperm cells
• Correct pH between 6.4 to 6.9

subQuestions.questionText: The diagram shows a type of cloning (showing Donor cell with removed nucleus (A), Somatic body cell, fusion, In vitro blastocyst development, Embryonic stem cells → Cultured stem cells). Identify the type of cloning in the diagram above.
subQuestions.memoText:
Answer (1 mark):
Therapeutic cloning

subQuestions.questionText: Indicate the purpose of performing the cloning in QUESTION 4.5.1.
subQuestions.memoText:
Answer (1 mark):
Produce embryonic stem cells that can be used for cell therapy / develop new animal treatments

subQuestions.questionText: Name the process that has resulted in cell A.
subQuestions.memoText:
Answer (1 mark):
Enucleation

subQuestions.questionText: Give a reason for the process named in QUESTION 4.5.3.
subQuestions.memoText:
Answer (1 mark):
To prevent the genetic material of an egg cell from interfering with the process

subQuestions.questionText: The picture illustrates a stage of parturition (showing a cow with a calf emerging during birth). Indicate the stage of parturition in the picture above.
subQuestions.memoText:
Answer (1 mark):
Ejection / expulsion of the foetus

subQuestions.questionText: Name the stage that follows the one in QUESTION 4.6.1.
subQuestions.memoText:
Answer (1 mark):
Ejection / expulsion of placenta

subQuestions.questionText: State ONE factor that will make it difficult for the cow to get into the stage named in QUESTION 4.6.2.
subQuestions.memoText:
Any 1 of the following (1 mark):
• Deficiency of vitamin A
• Diseases / infections in the reproductive tract
• Exhaustion
• Mineral deficiencies
• Hereditary defects
• Over-conditioning of cows
• Inertia of the uterus
• Metabolic disorders
• Failure of the foetal membranes and maternal tissues to break after parturition
• Use of hormones to induce parturition
• Dystocia / prolonged labour
• Hormonal imbalances
• Multiple births / twinning

subQuestions.questionText: Name ONE calf-related problem that may interfere with the normal parturition process.
subQuestions.memoText:
Any 1 of the following (1 mark):
• High birth weight
• Malformed foetus / deformities
• Deviation of the head
• Flexion of the elbow
• Retention of one or both forelegs
• Hydrocephalus
• Hydrops Fetalis
• Posterior presentation
• Multiple births / twinning
• Death of the foetus
